title: perf-bench-scratch-noah-garcia-2026-03-03
content:
Quick scratchpad for perf runs (notes + raw numbers)
Owner: Noah Garcia (eng-serving-runtime)
Collaborators: Maya Lopez, Ethan Wang
Last run: 2026-03-02 (see runs below)

Environment:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (DGX, shared test pool)
- Runtime: Redwood serving-runtime v0.9.2 (local dev cluster)
- CUDA: 12.1, cuDNN: 9.0, NCCL: 2.18
- Python: 3.10, PyTorch: 2.2.1, Triton kernels enabled
- Model: Llama2-13B (gptq q4_0) tokenized with sentencepiece v1.0
- KV cache: enabled for decode runs unless stated otherwise
- Notes: warmup 10 requests, heat stabilization for 2 minutes before capture

Purpose: understand latency/throughput tradeoffs across seq lengths and batching; verify KV cache speedups and regression from latest kernel change (kernel-selection v0.9.2).

Run summary (2026-03-02):
Config common to table: model=Llama2-13B gptq4, device=A100-80GB, single stream unless batch specified. p50/p90/p99 in ms, tok/s measured over 60s steady window (summed tokens / wall time).

Seq | Batch | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | tok/s
------------------------------------------------
128 | 1 | 45 | 60 | 120 | 2800
512 | 1 | 120 | 200 | 400 | 1800
2048 | 1 | 420 | 700 | 1200 | 1300
8192 | 1 | 1600 | 2500 | 3500 | 900

512 | 4 | 90 | 160 | 320 | 5200
512 | 8 | 110 | 210 | 420 | 7600

Notes on table: single-request latency grows roughly linearly with sequence length (expected). Batch helps throughput significantly but increases p50 slightly due to queueing. Batch=4 is sweet spot for seq512 (tok/s ~5200) on this HW profile. Batch=8 shows diminishing returns for latency-sensitive flows.

Effect of KV cache (decode scenarios):
- Prefix reuse workload: 512-token prefix + streaming decode of 128 tokens. With KV cache on: p50 decode step ~12ms, tok/s ~6500 (amortized). Without KV cache: first decode step includes full prefix compute: p50 ~140ms for same call, tok/s ~1700.
- Conclusion: KV cache yields 3-4x token/sec improvement for iterative decoding; critical for chat-like workloads.

Quantization impact quick check (A/B):
- q4_0 (gptq): base throughput used above.
- 8-bit (int8 simulated): ~+15-20% tok/s over q4_0 for seq<=512, but memory pressure higher for long seqs and batch>4 (OOM observed at batch=8, seq=2048 in one run).
- FP16 (baseline): ~-25% tok/s vs q4_0 in these runs (expected due to kernel optimizations for int4 paths).

Observed anomalies / regressions:
- Kernel-selection change in v0.9.2 increased p99 for seq2048 by ~10% vs v0.9.1 in quick diff. Need to reproduce with stable config and smaller noise window.
- One run showed occasional p99 spikes coincident with background NVLink congestion on host (cross-tenant test cluster). Re-run on isolated node planned.

Quick conclusions / action items:
- Batch=4 for seq512 is good default for internal throughput SLOs; document as recommended config for dedicated pools.
- KV cache must be enabled by default for chat endpoints; add a test gating accuracy of cache state across rollouts.
- Investigate kernel-selection v0.9.2 p99 uplift: bisect between v0.9.1 and v0.9.2, capture perf counters. (assigned to Ethan)
- Add a long-run stability test (6hr soak) on isolated A100 node to surface rare p99 spikes. (Maya to schedule)
- Add automated smoke comparing q4_0 vs int8 memory/OOM behavior for batch>=4 and seq>=2048.

Raw run notes (timestamps UTC):
- 2026-03-02T02:10: warmup, 10 requests. steady capture started 02:12.
- 2026-03-02T02:18: seq512 batch4 captured 60s window: avg tokens/s 5204, p50 88ms, p90 158ms.
- 2026-03-02T02:26: seq2048 batch1 capture 60s: tokens/s 1296, p50 418ms, p99 spike ~1250ms (one sample).
- 2026-03-02T02:35: reproduce on isolated node: p99 spike dropped, suggests cross-tenant interference.

Notes-to-self: include these artifacts when filing PERF-1234: raw CSVs, flamegraphs, nvprof traces for the p99 cases, and the kernel-selection config. Keep runs reproducible: add run-id header to capture outputs.

Next runs planned:
- 2026-03-04: long-soak 6hr seq512 batch4 isolated node (collect p95/p99 over time buckets)
- 2026-03-05: kernel-selection bisect between v0.9.1 & v0.9.2 (Ethan)

Scratch list (todo):
- [ ] Export CSVs from /tmp/perf_runs/* and attach to Jira INF-4567
- [ ] Create short internal doc summarizing recommended defaults for Dedicated pools (batching + kv-cache)
- [ ] Add perf test to CI that fails if p99 increases >15% vs baseline

End of scratchpad.
